name: Liangzhu
place: the Yangtze delta, around Lake Tai
desc: Rice farmers of the Yangtze delta who built a walled city on the water, protected by the oldest large dams in the world, and carved jade tubes and discs with a staring god-and-beast face that no one has fully explained.
source: Excavations at Liangzhu, Yuhang (from 1936), including the Mojiaoshan palace platform and the dam system; a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2019

cautious: packed reed-wrapped bundles of clay into the dam until it held
gluttonous: filled the storage pits with enough rice for three years
devout: carved the god's staring eyes on a jade tube

inventions.name: High and Low Dams
inventions.source: Eleven dams north-west of Liangzhu, built around 3100 BCE of clay packed in reed bundles, held back floods and stored water
inventions.desc: Walls of clay in reed bags across the valleys, to hold back the mountain floods and keep water for the dry months: farm plots yield 25% more, +1 defence.
inventions.hint: Needs farming and the Tribe & Agrarian Era.

inventions.name: Jade Cong and Bi
inventions.source: Square jade tubes (cong) and flat discs (bi) carved with the 'god-man-beast' face; the largest cong, from Fanshan tomb M12, weighs 6.5 kg
inventions.desc: A square tube with a round hole, and a flat disc with a hole, carved with a god riding a beast: rites bring 15% more devotion, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs jade and Polished Stone Tools.

inventions.name: Rice Paddies
inventions.source: Field systems at Maoshan near Liangzhu, with ridges and canals, show large-scale paddy farming
inventions.desc: Flooded fields divided by low banks, with water let in and out by little canals: farm plots yield 15% more.

inventions.name: Great Rice Store
inventions.source: A pit beside the Mojiaoshan palace held some 200,000 kg of burnt rice
inventions.desc: Pits and halls for the rice of the whole delta: the stores hold 40 more food.

foods.name: Steamed Rice
foods.desc: Rice steamed soft in a pottery steamer: hunger grows 10% slower.

foods.name: Water Caltrop and Lotus Root
foods.source: Water caltrop and lotus remains are common at Liangzhu and Hemudu sites
foods.desc: Horned nuts from the ponds and crunchy lotus roots, boiled together: hunger grows 5% slower, food spoils 5% slower.

finds.name: Wild Rice
finds.desc: Rice grass in the wet margins of the lakes. Gathering it brings farming closer.

finds.name: Water Caltrop
finds.desc: Floating plants with horned nuts, picked from boats.

finds.name: Mountain Jade
finds.desc: Pale green jade from the hills to the west: each load is lore.

people.name: Tang Yuan
people.desc: He has watched the floods come down the valleys for forty years.
memory: closed the gap in the dam an hour before the flood came

people.name: Yao Ling
people.desc: She alone may hold the great cong at the rites.
memory: held up the great cong to the sky at the summer rite

people.name: The King of Cong
people.source: Tomb M12 at Fanshan, the richest Liangzhu burial, with the largest jade cong and a jade axe of command
people.desc: A ruler buried with over six hundred jades, including the greatest cong ever found and a jade axe carved with the god.

people.name: The God Riding the Beast
people.source: The 'god-man-beast' emblem carved on Liangzhu jades
people.desc: A feathered figure riding a beast with huge round eyes: the god of Liangzhu, carved on every great jade, whose name is lost.

people.name: Chuan
people.text: a trader who poles a dugout boat through the delta channels, carrying jade, salt and stories from the coast.
memory: poled a boat through every channel of the delta in one summer
people.desc: A boatman of the water towns.

people.name: Mo Shan
people.label: Mo Shan, Lord of the Waters
people.desc: He commands the floods to stop, and they do. Crafting 8, Lore 5.

people.name: Shen Hui
people.label: Shen Hui, Face of the God
people.desc: She wears the god's face at the rites. Lore 8.

people.name: Yue
people.label: Yue, Bearer of the Jade Axe
people.desc: He carries the axe that means command. Combat 8.

events.title: Wall the Valleys
events.text: The mountain floods came down again and drowned the lower fields. The builders want to wall off the valleys above the city with clay in reed bags.

options.label: Build the dams
options.result: Thousands of reed bags of clay, stacked by thousands of hands. The next flood stops at the wall.

options.label: Move to higher ground
options.result: The low fields are left to the water.

events.title: The Water Will Not Go Down
events.source: A layer of flood silt over Liangzhu around 2300 BCE marks the end of the city
events.text: This flood is not like the others. The water stands in the city for months, and mud covers the fields. Some say the god has turned his face away.

options.label: Stay and dig out
options.result: Season after season the mud is cleared. The city lives on, smaller.

options.label: Scatter to the hills
options.result: The people leave the water city. Their jades travel north, and the god's face is carved for a thousand years more.

events.title: The Great Platform
events.source: The Mojiaoshan platform, an artificial mound about 30 hectares across, carried the palaces of Liangzhu
events.text: The chief wants the palace raised on a great platform of earth above the flood, the biggest thing anyone has ever built.

options.label: Raise the platform
options.result: Year after year the platform rises. From its top, the whole delta can be seen.

options.label: Not now
options.result: The palace stays where it is.

tales.name: The God with Round Eyes
tales.source: A story made up around the Liangzhu emblem
tales.text: Long ago a feathered god came down riding a great beast with eyes like full moons. Where the beast looked, the floods drew back and the rice grew. So we carve its eyes on every jade, so that it keeps looking at our fields.

tales.name: Why the Cong Is Square Outside and Round Inside
tales.source: A story made up around the jade cong
tales.text: The earth is square and the sky is round. The cong is square outside and round inside, so that the earth can hold the sky within it. When the priest holds the cong up, the sky comes down into the tube and speaks.

tales.name: The Rice and the Fish
tales.source: A story in the manner of the water towns
tales.text: Rice and Fish lived in the same pond. Fish said: your roots muddy my water. Rice said: your tail knocks my stems. So the god divided them, and the rice died of weeds and the fish died of hunger. The god put them back together, and since then they live as friends.

tales.name: The Boat Race on the Lake
tales.source: A story made up around the water towns of the delta
tales.text: At midsummer every village launches its longest dugout, painted with the god's eyes, and the young men race across the lake. The winning village holds the great jade disc for a year.
tales.moral: the lake belongs to all the villages
